{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal Team  
**From:** In-House Counsel  
**Re:** Playbook review of Master Services Agreement (Customer-side)

---

## Executive Summary

We have reviewed the Master Services Agreement against our playbook. The document is, on the whole, unusually favourable to us: indemnification (§ 20), IP and data ownership (§ 14), licence scope (§ 13), assignment and change of control (§ 24), termination for convenience (§ 9), audit rights (§ 22), transition assistance (§ 11), renewal mechanics (§ 8), governing law (§ 28), insurance (§ 18) and the absence of exclusivity, non-compete, MFN and minimum-commitment obligations on Customer all meet or exceed our preferred positions and require no redline.

Three items require attention:

1. **Limitation of liability cap basis (§ 21) — critical.** The cap is mutual and the carve-outs are strong, but "Fees" is defined at § 1.5 as the Implementation Fee, fixed at a one-time USD 12,000 under § 1.6. The "twelve months preceding" cap is therefore illusory (approximately USD 12,000) and sits far below our walk-away floor of six months' charges.
2. **Customer-payable liquidated damages (§ 7.7) — high.** Liquidated damages of 15% of annual Fees per week of delay after a ten-day grace period breach our position that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer, and would compound rapidly beyond remaining contract value.
3. **Warranty duration and remedy (§ 19) — medium.** Software Deliverables carry only ninety days (we require twelve months), and the § 19.4 refund is tied to the narrow "Fees" definition, hollowing out the repair/replace/refund remedy.

One finding (non-solicitation, § 12) is flagged **needs review** on verification and should be confirmed before we close the file, notwithstanding that the substantive conclusion is that no non-solicitation covenant binds Customer.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | Deviation | § 21 Limitation of Liability |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 Indemnification |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 Intellectual Property and Deliverables |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Deviation | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 Assignment and Change of Control |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 Access Rights and Licence |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 Termination |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation (redline repaired) | § 19 Warranties |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Needs review (verification failed) | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 Audit Rights |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 8 Term and Renewal |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 Transition Assistance and Data Return |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 Insurance |

---

## Walk-Away Items

Two deviations sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature:

- **§ 21 — cap basis.** The effective cap of approximately USD 12,000 falls far below our walk-away floor of six months' charges. Our redline restates the basis as the greater of (a) all amounts paid or payable by Customer under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding twelve months and (b) USD 1,000,000, leaving mutuality and the § 21.3 Excluded Claims untouched.
- **§ 7.7 — Customer-payable liquidated damages.** Liquidated damages compounding at 15% of annual Fees per week would rapidly exceed remaining contract value, which the playbook identifies as walk-away territory. We propose deletion; simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts is an acceptable substitute.

---

## Next Steps

1. **Issue the redlines** on § 21 (cap basis) and § 7.7 (deletion of liquidated damages), flagging both to Vendor as conditions of signature rather than negotiable preferences.
2. **Issue the § 19 warranty redline**: express the Deliverable conformance period numerically, extend it to twelve (12) months for software Deliverables and ninety (90) days for all other Deliverables, and untie the § 19.4 refund from the narrow "Fees" definition by referring to all amounts paid for the non-conforming item. Fallback if Vendor resists: retain ninety days for all Deliverables provided the refund fix is accepted. Alternative on the refund point: broaden the § 1.5 definition of "Fees".
3. **Consider a definitional fix at § 1.5.** The narrow "Fees" definition (Implementation Fee only, USD 12,000 per § 1.6) drives both the § 21 and § 19.4 defects. Broadening it at source may be the cleanest single change and should be raised with Vendor as an option.
4. **Close out the NOSOLICIT finding.** The substantive conclusion is that no non-solicitation or no-hire covenant binds Customer, and § 12.3 affirmatively preserves our freedom to hire respondents to general recruitment. Verification nonetheless failed, so we should re-run the check and confirm before sign-off. No redline is appropriate: inserting duration or general-solicitation carve-out language would first require creating a restrictive covenant against us.
5. **No action required** on the remaining fourteen compliant findings; we will not reopen provisions that already meet or exceed our preferred positions."}
